title: B300 KDA prefill needs chunk-resident state and stateful native lowering before a scalar route can close the measured gap
backend: native_cuda and cutlass_cute_dsl component admission; B300 adapted CAKE M64 external reference
executor_revision: B300-M4 agent-gpu-broker 0.6.0 custom diagnostic; no formal sm_103a Executor receipt

evidence.note: A separate exact-sm_103a diagnostic port of the pinned B200 CAKE export compiled both M64 and M128 without GPU visibility. Only the host target gate and compilation architecture changed; this is not the original B200 qualification.
M64 fixed H64/T65 full-chunk-plus-tail output 532480/532480 and in-place state 1048576/1048576 passed the independent CPU recurrence at atol=rtol=0.01; all immutable inputs were unchanged.
M128 packed H96 lengths 33,65,17 with seq_order [1,0,2] passed all 1413120 output and 4718592 final-state elements and preserved immutable inputs.
The adapted reference passed the complete H64/T8192 benchmark-shape CPU oracle: 67108864 output and 1048576 final-state elements, zero tolerance failures, and every immutable input unchanged.

Five broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds with distinct initial-state slots per invocation measured the adapted one-kernel reference at 456.034 microseconds median; maximum within-round CV was 0.117%. Each round retained complete output/state and passed the external CPU oracle. No B200-paper comparison is made.

A direct register-resident per-token native CUDA prototype, outside Compiler admission, passed the complete H64/T65 output and state oracle. NVCC reported 71 registers and zero spills. An earlier host-only target-name refusal was retained as a failed broker job before this successor.
The same native prototype passed every H64/T8192 output and final-state element with unchanged inputs; its correctness cannot establish useful performance.

Five paired broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds measured adapted CAKE reference 456.195 versus scalar prototype 16979.920 microseconds, median paired scalar/reference 37.220750x. Both arms had exactly one CUDA activity, zero oracle failures and maximum within-round CV 0.135%/0.082%. This is a bounded mechanism diagnostic, not a Cake candidate or formal Evaluation.

Retargeted component probes on sm_103a show simple Triton state source lowers; CuTe state refuses CUTE_STATE_UNSUPPORTED, CuTe TMEM witness refuses CUTE_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED, and native state refuses NATIVE_BUFFER_REFINEMENT_UNSUPPORTED plus load/store ownership refinements. A small native TMA/MMA pipeline witness lowers, but no complete KDA Schedule is admitted.

The committed chunk-32 algebra at dca6ac1d passed all 67108864 output and 1048576 final-state elements against the independent recurrence on the exact H64/T8192 B300 prepared inputs; local BF16-quantized matrix-operand simulation also passed. This validates the mathematical candidate, not its GPU mapping.

An unadmitted one-program-per-head-and-64-V-row Triton chunk-32 prototype compiled for sm_103a. Static cubin inspection reported 128 registers, 176 bytes of stack per thread and 66 local load/store SASS instructions. These facts support a spill/resource-pressure hypothesis, not a dynamic bottleneck attribution.
The unadmitted Triton chunk prototype passed the independent complete H64/T65 output and final-state oracle with immutable inputs unchanged.
The same prototype passed every H64/T8192 output and final-state element at atol=rtol=0.01 with immutable inputs unchanged.

Five paired broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds measured adapted CAKE reference 456.035 versus unadmitted Triton chunk prototype 96080.520 microseconds, median paired candidate/reference 210.686724x. Both one-kernel arms passed the full oracle each round; maximum within-round CV was 0.108%/0.479%. This negative mechanism diagnostic is neither a qualified Cake candidate nor formal Evaluation.

A smaller unadmitted chunk-16, V-tile-32 Triton variant compiled offline for sm_103a; cubin inspection reported 238 registers, zero stack bytes and no static local SASS accesses. This removes the observed static spill signal but has not established runtime speed.
The smaller variant passed complete H64/T65 output and final-state CPU oracle checks with all immutable inputs unchanged.
The smaller variant also passed all H64/T8192 output and final-state elements at atol=rtol=0.01 with unchanged immutable inputs.

Five same-run broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds measured adapted CAKE reference 456.259 versus unadmitted chunk-16/V-tile-32 Triton 83264.993 microseconds; median paired candidate/reference 182.495015x. Every complete output/state check passed, each arm had one CUDA activity, and maximum within-round CV was 0.144%/0.202%. A predecessor job gpuq-76a2113101cd was refused before launch by the source-commit identity guard and retained as failed evidence. Removing the static spill signal improves latency only modestly; the remaining gap is not uniquely attributed.

Native CUDA's bounded global-state read/modify/write admission at cdaba6c3 passed 47 native contracts and the 179-case Corpus Gate from a clean fixed-commit worktree. An in-place GEMM state Schedule retains one global state argument and checks read-before-MMA-before-store; verifier counterexamples still refuse owner drift and a state store inside the contraction loop. This does not admit KDA's TMEM-resident state.

The emitted native CUDA in-place state witness compiled offline for exact sm_103a with 103 registers and no spills, then passed a broker-shared B300 device check on three independent scales/seeds. Each case matched all 131072 output-state elements within atol=rtol=0.01, changed the caller's state in place and preserved both input matrices. This qualifies a prerequisite mechanism only; it is neither KDA correctness nor KDA performance evidence.

An unadmitted exact-sm_103a native PTX probe packs BF16 row pairs into 32-bit words, writes 128x64 state through tcgen05.st.sync.aligned.32x32b.x8, waits for stores, then reads it through tcgen05.ld and waits for loads. Three 8192-element distributions round-tripped bitwise with input unchanged. Offline NVCC reported 40 registers and zero spills. This proves the isolated register/TMEM copy atom and wait sequence, not tensor-operand MMA or complete KDA state residency.

A separate unadmitted PTX witness packs BF16 state into TMEM, waits for store completion, uses that TMEM tile as tcgen05.mma operand A against a swizzled shared-memory B tile, commits and waits for the MMA, then reads FP32 TMEM output. Three independent 128x64 by 64x64 cases passed all 8192 output elements at atol=rtol=0.01 with maximum absolute error 5.722e-6 and both inputs unchanged. Offline NVCC reported 30 registers, zero stack/spills and an exact-sm_103a cubin. This proves the isolated TMEM-A MMA path on B300, not a KDA chunk update or performance edge.

The isolated task/nvidia-tmem-state-prototype combined the core typed TMEM-store/TMEM-A contract with native CUDA emission and an exact-sm_103a Target declaration. At clean commit e47c78ab, the full CPU contracts passed 2517 tests with 26 skips, and all 179 Corpus Gate cases matched without regenerating expectations. A later documentation-only successor aa5fad67 passed 53 affected tests. This is a local prototype branch; neither its generated source nor its new Target admission has passed NVCC or B300 device validation.

The Compiler emitted a complete single-CTA source from tmem-state-mma-witness on sm_103a: register BF16 load, x8 TMEM store, four-arrival completion, TMA B staging, barrier wait and fence before TMEM-A tcgen05 MMA, FP32 TMEM readout and global store. Public assessment was lowerable and the source was retained for exact-target compilation. Structural emission and CPU contracts are not compile or device evidence.

A two-chunk recurrence-shaped Schedule at fixed compiler e47c78ab tested one pre-loop BF16 TMEM initialization and one in-loop update of the same tensor tile. Common assessment refused BUFFER_MULTIPLE_WRITERS at a_tmem and TMEM_STORE_COMPLETION_OWNERSHIP at state_ready; direct native preflight additionally refused the loop pipeline body, TMEM-A contraction scope, completion consumer lifetime and in-loop TMEM store. The retained schedule isolates a missing loop-carried state effect and per-chunk barrier phase for this route; it does not prove every possible Cake formulation impossible.

A separate core task branch added TileLoop.carried_buffers with a bounded proof of one pre-loop BF16 TMEM initializer, one per-trip updater, ordered readers and a four-arrival barrier. On clean f9a69c86, 64 affected contracts, all 179 Corpus Gate cases, and the full 2509-test CPU contract suite passed with 26 skips. The formerly refused two-chunk probe passes common verification only when it declares the carry; without it the original multiple-writer and barrier refusals remain. This is a local IR tick, not NVIDIA emission qualification.

The isolated NVIDIA integration prototype now emits a static carried two-chunk TMEM state recurrence with per-trip TMA B staging, TMEM-A MMA, FP32 readout, BF16 state update and alternating mbarrier parity. At clean 65424e4c, 98 affected contracts, 179 Corpus Gate cases and the full 2522-test CPU contract suite passed with 26 skips. A later stage-depth refusal and four-chunk parity boundary passed their affected tests. Generated CUDA has not been compiled or launched on B300 because SSH 10.27.2.17:22 timed out.

A clean-commit public Compiler lowering retained the two-chunk native source and its exact-sm_103a toolchain requirements (one CTA, six warps, 8240 shared bytes) alongside a broker-aware independent two-chunk BF16 recurrence checker. This fixed source is ready for CPU-only NVCC compilation followed by B300 device validation; source inspection does not establish either.

A separate native CUDA prototype adds row-owned FP32 exp, rsqrt, reciprocal, SUM over a register row and proven scalar-per-row broadcast. It keeps a replicated vector of the same rank and extent from masquerading as row-owned. At clean 5ea8ed6b, 70 affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases passed; the full CPU contract suite passed 2526 tests with 26 skips. Generated math is not a KDA Workload candidate or B300 numerical evidence.

A follow-up row-normalization witness widens the local sum and broadcast to KDA's full 128-element head dimension. Clean be8a21ed passed 62 affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases; exact-sm_103a generated source and a broker-aware numerical checker are retained. NVCC compilation and B300 correctness remain pending because SSH still times out.

A separate core ScanOp.MUL tick uses the existing typed inclusive scan with FP32 accumulation and Triton tl.cumprod, preserving sum and reverse directions. At clean 3bcc133d, 85 affected contracts, all 179 Corpus Gate cases and the full 2502-test CPU contract suite passed with 26 skips. Native CUDA still refuses scan by name; no GPU prefix numerics or latency are implied.

The isolated NVIDIA prototype composes g, A_log and dt_bias into a typed exact-sm_103a H64/T8192 32-token decay-prefix Triton stage. Clean d5f95196 passed 58 affected contracts, 179 Corpus Gate cases and the full 2531-test CPU contract suite with 26 skips. Its FP32 prefix output is 256 MiB; a WorkBound traffic screen gives a 50.336 us ideal bandwidth floor at the Target-declared peak, excludes exponential/scan cost and is not measured time. The retained broker-aware full-output checker has not run on B300.

A separate CPU chunk-algebra screen rounds each 32-token prefix to BF16 before its use. Against independent complete T65 and T257 KDA recurrence oracles, all 532480 and 2105344 output elements plus 1048576 final-state elements in each case passed at atol=rtol=0.01. This is a numerical feasibility screen only; it does not qualify the full H64/T8192 shape or a GPU mapping.

An explicit BF16 prefix-output variant keeps FP32 scan arithmetic but halves stored prefix bytes to 128 MiB. Clean 396314f4 passed five affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases; its analytic compulsory-traffic floor is 33.559 us at the declared peak. Generated source and a broker-aware complete H64/T8192 prefix checker are retained. Neither variant has B300 device correctness or timing evidence.

A matrix-form solve of the strict lower-triangular 32-token correction passed complete T65 and T257 output/final-state oracles. A five-step doubling solve using BF16-rounded matrix operands and FP32 accumulation also passed the independent H64/T8192 token oracle on same-distribution NumPy inputs: zero failures among 67108864 output and 1048576 final-state elements, maximum absolute errors 0.0001221 and 0.0004883. It is a numerical screen, not a tensor-core implementation or GPU speed result.

A stronger combined full H64/T8192 CPU screen replaces direct decay products with log-domain intervening factors, rounds each 32-token prefix to BF16, and solves updates by five BF16-operand/FP32-accumulation doubling steps. The independent per-token oracle still reports zero tolerance failures over every output and final-state element (maximum absolute errors 0.0001221 and 0.0004883). These are same-distribution NumPy inputs rather than the exact prepared B300 bytes; the retained script and report select a GPU hypothesis only.

The five-step BF16-operand inverse factor can be computed before state-dependent RHS and stored as BF16. One extra BF16-operand/FP32-accumulation inverse-times-RHS product passed the independent complete H64/T8192 token oracle with zero output/state failures (max_abs 0.0001221/0.0009766); T65/T257 guardrails also passed. A dual-view version maintaining each factor and its transpose for Cake A-times-B-transpose MMAs passed the same full and guardrail checks. These screens do not include GPU launch, traffic or resource cost.

A typed exact-sm_103a Cake Triton component unrolls the dual-view inverse into 18 explicit BF16 MMA operations and emits a 32 MiB BF16 factor for all H64/T8192 chunks. Clean 2d0adc91 passed 13 affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases; retained source, full Schedule, independent strictly-lower-matrix checker and WorkBound screen are outside checkout. Its two 32 MiB inputs must be a matrix/transpose pair produced consistently upstream. The 19.327 billion logical MMA FLOPs and 12.583 us ideal compulsory-traffic floor are analytic, not device results; compilation, spills, correctness and latency remain unverified.

A midpoint-scaled log-decay factorization turns each 32-token prediction/output coupling into BF16-operand matrix products instead of per-pair sequential decay products. The factor split bounds both exponent signs to half the within-chunk log-decay span under the fixed lower_bound=-5 and chunk32. Combined with BF16 prefix storage and dual-view BF16 triangular inverse, the independent same-distribution H64/T8192 token oracle passed all 67108864 output and 1048576 final-state elements (max_abs 0.0001221/0.0009766); T65/T257 guardrails also passed. No Cake/GPU coupling producer or performance receipt exists.

A held-out T65/H64 constant g=-20 input (decay effectively one) exposed final-state failures despite all output elements passing. The original serial chunk32/FP32 algebra already failed 2458/1048576 state elements; BF16 precomputed inverse failed 2606 and midpoint BF16 coupling 2619. Thus the new matrix factorization is not the primary cause. The ordinary Workload inputs were not changed.

On the same high-retention input, chunk1 matched the independent BF16 final state exactly while chunk2/4/8/16/32 all had final-state tolerance failures. A constant-gate sweep passed at g=-4 (decay about 0.914) but had 123 failures at g=-6 (decay about 0.988), and more at stronger retention. This supports omitted per-token BF16 state rounding as the high-retention limitation; it supplies no proven dispatch threshold or B300 speed result.

A typed exact-sm_103a Triton component takes BF16 normalized Q/K plus FP32 per-token log-decay, scans 32-token log prefixes, extracts first/last rows with coordinate masks and reductions, and emits midpoint-scaled forward/backward BF16 factors. Clean 68c5f94c passed nine affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases; source and complete synthetic-factor checker are retained. Its three 128 MiB factor outputs and 512 MiB declared inputs are analytic traffic, not qualified B300 time or a complete KDA stage.

A second typed exact-sm_103a component uses three existing BF16 MMA nodes, strict triangular masks and explicit beta row/column broadcasts to emit prediction coupling P, transposed PT and output correction B. Clean a9056071 passed seven affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases; source, synthetic-input complete-output checker and WorkBound report are retained. Its pre-scaled factor inputs are produced only by the preceding unqualified component; there is no fused or device-validated KDA pipeline.

Summing the four separately materialized prefix/factor/coupling/inverse WorkBound projections gives 1.143 GB logical input and 0.671 GB logical output bytes before the state kernel, with a 226.76 us sum of individual peak-bandwidth screens. Cache reuse, overlap, instruction cost and launches are not modeled, so this is neither a measured runtime nor an additive lower bound. It selects fusion and reduced intermediate traffic as the next performance hypothesis, not a speedup claim.

A typed exact-sm_103a upstream component composes full-128 BF16 Q/K normalization, FP32 log-decay and FP32 beta sigmoid from the public Q/K/G/beta/A_log/dt_bias inputs. Clean 19e6e77b passed 11 affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases; generated source, complete prepared-H64/T8192 broker checker and WorkBound screen are retained. Its four preparation outputs are not the public KDA result; no B300 compilation, correctness or timing exists.

A four-component upstream/factor/coupling/inverse WorkBound screen counts 1.412 GB logical input and 1.076 GB logical output bytes before the state kernel. Three adjacent materialization boundaries account for about 2.013 GB write-then-read bytes that a valid fusion could eliminate; the sum of individual peak-bandwidth screens is 311.04 us. Cache, overlap, instruction cost, launches and on-chip capacity are unmodeled, so no additive runtime lower bound or winning implementation follows. This prioritizes measured fusion experiments over stacking all components as a claimed speedup.

One typed Triton Schedule fuses upstream Q/K normalization and gates, midpoint factors and three coupling MMAs, passing register values across former global stage boundaries. Clean a6e76f14 passed 10 affected contracts, all 179 Corpus Gate cases and the full 2542-test CPU suite with 26 skips. The emitted exact-sm_103a component declares about 404 MB logical input and 101 MB output rather than the separate-stage intermediate traffic, but NVCC/Triton resource compilation and B300 correctness/timing remain absent.

A distinct fused-depth variant keeps P/PT on chip and executes 21 explicit BF16 MMAs in one typed Schedule, returning only B and inverse. Clean 73ba9819 passed six affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases. Its 404/67 MB logical input/output is analytic and omits state-kernel preparation operands; the dependent MMA chain may spill or serialize, so it cannot be selected without device compilation and paired timing.

A seven-output successor adds the BF16 base-key, base-query and final-key tiles plus FP32 beta_gate and prefix_end needed by the native state consumer. At clean 257ec49b, six affected contracts, all 179 Corpus Gate cases and the full 2546-test CPU suite passed with 26 skips. The generated source declares about 404 MB input and 480 MB output, before state-kernel traffic; no GPU compilation or measurement exists.

A separate CPU consumer of exactly those seven preparation outputs takes only V and current BF16 recurrent state, then reconstructs complete KDA outputs and final in-place state. Independent per-token oracle comparisons passed all T65, T257 and same-distribution H64/T8192 elements (67108864 output and 1048576 state in the full case; max_abs 0.0002441/0.0009766). This proves the numerical ABI is sufficient, not that Cake has emitted the native state kernel or met the exact B300 prepared bytes.

A V-row formulation places all five state-dependent products on dynamic MMA A: base prediction/output, inverse-times-RHS, output correction and final state correction. The seven prepared values are reoriented as static MMA B operands; a separate CPU consumer passed independent per-token T65, T257 and same-distribution H64/T8192 output/state oracles (full 67,108,864 output and 1,048,576 state elements, zero tolerance failures). This source audit and numerical proof removes the suspected register-to-shared staging requirement for these products; existing generated preparation outputs and native pipeline are not yet reoriented, compiled or GPU qualified.

Correction to event 50 physical layout: Cake native CUDA models tcgen05 B as [N,K] and computes A[M,K] @ B[N,K].T, while that earlier CPU screen used conventional B [K,N]. Re-derived the seven-output interface under the actual backend contract. Base-key/query [C,128], B/inverse [C,C] stay in their original orientation; only final-key becomes [128,C]. Independent token-oracle T65, T257 and same-distribution H64/T8192 output/state all pass (full 67,108,864 output and 1,048,576 state elements, zero tolerance failures). A source-only native preflight counterexample reports NATIVE_SMEM_LAYOUT for a BF16 K128 B row of 256 bytes; current B staging is limited to a 128-byte swizzle row. This is not B300 device proof or a complete state kernel.

Clean prototype 269cb1c2 emits a 21-MMA typed Triton preprocessing source for the corrected native B[N,K] interface: base-key/query, B and inverse retain their original storage orientation, while final-key is explicitly transposed. The separate T65/T257/full H64 CPU consumer passes the independent oracle. At clean b19798fd, 25 affected contracts and all 179 Corpus Gate cases pass; Python syntax compilation passes. The emitted source has no Triton AOT/B300 correctness or timing result and is not a complete KDA kernel.

The current native CUDA preflight and a dedicated counterexample establish a local NATIVE_SMEM_LAYOUT refusal for BF16 K128 base-key/query B rows (256 bytes versus its modeled 128-byte maximum). NVIDIA CUTLASS documentation supports MN-major B as a hardware mode, but Cake does not implement its descriptor/TMA/emission route; explicit K64 split staging is a second design. Neither is selected without an exact-B300 numerical/device probe. This is a backend capability gate, not an oracle failure or measured speed result.

Cake-emitted root TMEM-A BF16 MMA at fixed source e47c78ab compiled for exact sm_103a with 72 registers and zero stack/spills. Broker-shared B300 device check passed all 8192 outputs for each of seeds 13, 71 and 181 against independent FP32 matmul (max abs 5.722e-6); both immutable inputs were bitwise unchanged. Broker reports completed exit 0 and no retained lease. This is a bounded MMA witness, not KDA.

Cake-emitted two-chunk loop-carried TMEM state witness at fixed source 65424e4c compiled exact sm_103a with 101 registers and zero stack/spills. Broker-shared B300 check passed all 8192 final output elements for each of seeds 13, 71 and 181 against CPU two-chunk recurrence (max abs 6.104e-5), preserving immutable inputs. Broker reports completed exit 0 and no retained lease. This qualifies the bounded carry mechanism, not full KDA recurrence.

Corrected seven-output Triton preprocessing source at fixed 269cb1c2 passed exact-sm_103a CPU-only AOT (32 KiB dynamic shared, 168 registers, zero local storage by cuobjdump). Broker-shared B300 device phase captured complete H64/T8192 outputs and preserved all immutable inputs; lease was released before host comparison. A v1 host report had an insufficient nonfinite-reference gate despite reporting pass; v2 replayed the same snapshots with explicit reference/observed nonfinite counts, all zero. Every element of all seven outputs passed atol=rtol=0.01 (three BF16 67,108,864-element tiles, two 16,777,216-element matrices, FP32 beta/prefix), no new GPU run for the v2 repair. This is preparation only, not complete KDA or timing.

A standalone edited PTX probe derived from the qualified TMEM-A witness stages physical B[K128,N32] in swizzle-64B shared memory, sets tcgen05 B-major bit, and advances descriptors by K16 x N32 x BF16 bytes. Exact-sm_103a NVCC compiled with 40 registers and zero spills; broker-shared B300 passed all 4096 output elements for each of three seeds versus independent FP32 A[128,128] @ B[128,32] (max abs 1.526e-5), with immutable inputs unchanged and released lease. This is hardware evidence for one MN-major mapping, not Cake backend admission or complete KDA.

The typed Cake MN-major B K128 witness emitted at clean 259062dc compiled exact-sm_103a with 40 registers and zero spills and passed broker-shared B300 checks: all 4096 FP32 output elements on each of seeds 13/71/181, zero tolerance failures, max abs 1.526e-5, finite output and immutable inputs. Broker reports completed exit 0 and released lease. The local core shape rule and NVIDIA emission passed focused contracts and Corpus Gate; this is one contraction, not the KDA state consumer.

Mixed-major seven-output fused Triton preparation at clean 5209294b passed CPU-only exact-sm_103a AOT (32 KiB shared, 227 registers, zero local storage) and broker-shared H64/T8192 device capture. After lease release, a strict host oracle checked every element of all seven outputs with zero failures and zero nonfinite reference/observed elements; all immutable inputs were unchanged. The mixed-major seven-output CPU consumer separately passed T65/T257/full H64 final output/state. This still omits the state consumer and timing.

The first broker-exclusive strict CUPTI attempt terminated before samples because the remote Python environment lacked cupti-python. The guard rejected CUDA-event fallback; broker reports failed exit 1 and released lease. cupti-python 13.0.1 was then installed into an isolated diagnostic directory, with CUDA 13.1 CUPTI library visibility checked before a new run. This failed attempt supports no latency claim.

Broker-exclusive exact-B300 CUPTI with cold L2, no CUDA graph, five rounds of 25 samples, one CUDA kernel, fully overwritten outputs and unchanged inputs measured the mixed-major preprocessing component at 637.606 us median of round medians; max within-round CV 0.125%. Broker reports completed exit 0 and released lease. This component alone exceeds the earlier adapted complete-reference diagnostic of 456.034 us, but those measurements were on separate jobs and are not a paired full-kernel speedup comparison. The 21-MMA materialized-preparation path therefore lacks headroom in this diagnostic; it must be redesigned before a complete KDA candidate can beat the reference.

Nsight Compute counter collection failed with ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM for this user; broker reports failed exit 1 and released lease. No counter or profiler bottleneck claim follows. CUPTI timing and compiled-resource reports remain available, but hardware-counter attribution requires host permission change by the owner or another qualified profiler path.

A corrected mixed-major seven-output CPU interface replaces explicit inverse preparation with strict-lower BF16 P and FP32 token-ordered forward substitution U_t=RHS_t+sum_{i<t}P[t,i]U_i, then BF16-rounds U for output/state contractions. Independent per-token T65, T257 and same-distribution H64/T8192 output/final-state checks pass at atol=rtol=0.01; full case covers 67,108,864 output and 1,048,576 state elements, zero failures. A first local run reached these comparisons but failed to write the report because the Mac disk was full; after deleting only this task’s completed detached test worktrees, the identical script was rerun and report writing succeeded. This is CPU numerical evidence, not GPU state-kernel execution.

Clean a6dc8c6d emits a two-BF16-MMA preparation Schedule for serial solve, omitting the 18-MMA explicit inverse and unused transpose branch. Exact-sm_103a AOT passes with 24 KiB dynamic shared, 185 registers and zero local storage. Broker-shared B300 captures all seven H64/T8192 outputs, preserves inputs and releases lease; strict host replay checks every P/B/base-key/base-query/final-key/beta/prefix element with zero tolerance failures and zero nonfinite reference/observed elements. No native state consumer or end-to-end result exists.

Broker-exclusive exact-B300 CUPTI cold-L2/no-graph diagnostic of the qualified two-MMA preparation component, five rounds x25 samples, single CUDA kernel and unchanged inputs, measured 389.507 us median of round medians, max within-round CV 0.179%; lease released. This is 248.099 us below the previous 637.606 us 21-MMA preparation diagnostic, but those are separate jobs. Compared with the earlier 456.034 us adapted complete-reference diagnostic in another job, only about 66.527 us of nonpaired latency headroom remains for a state consumer. No complete Cake KDA or paired speedup claim follows.

An unadmitted persistent Triton serial state-consumer v1 takes the qualified two-MMA P/B/base-key/query/final-key/beta/prefix outputs, V and the in-place BF16 state. CPU-only exact-sm_103a AOT compiled with 168 registers, 16,392 shared bytes, zero stack/local; broker-shared B300 captured all H64/T8192 output and final-state elements, preserved all immutable prepared inputs and state alias, then released its lease. Host-only independent oracle comparison passed all 67,108,864 output and 1,048,576 final-state elements at atol=rtol=0.01, zero nonfinite reference/observed and zero failures. This proves a complete fixed-shape mechanism, not Cake Scheduler admission, packed/high-retention generalization or speed.

First complete paired diagnostic stopped before candidate samples because the harness passed public q/k/g/beta [1,T,H,D] tensors to the fixed preparation component expecting [T,H,D]; reference round-one snapshots are retained, but the failed broker job supports no paired result. Broker reported failed exit 1 and released lease. A successor script uses shape-only contiguous views and preserves the Workload, source, oracle, CUPTI cold-L2/no-graph policy and independent state pools.

Broker-exclusive same-job five-round alternating-order complete H64/T8192 diagnostic compared the adapted CAKE reference (one CUDA activity) to Cake two-MMA preparation plus unadmitted persistent Triton serial consumer (two activities), with 25 strict CUPTI cold-L2/no-graph samples per arm/round and independent 512-slot initial states. Median paired candidate/reference latency ratio was 22.3619906724; round medians were reference 456.067/456.227/456.131/456.196/456.195 us and candidate 10198.566/10197.862/10199.621/10201.862/10202.789 us, max within-round CV 0.132%. After lease release, every saved round-last full output and final state for both arms passed the independent oracle with zero tolerance/nonfinite failures; inputs unchanged, broker completed exit 0, no retained lease. This is a correct but very slow unadmitted fixed-shape mechanism, not a Cake performance gain or formal Evaluation.

A standalone native CUDA/PTX forward-substitution probe stages each chunk/head strict-lower BF16 P in 2 KiB shared memory and gives each of 128 threads one V row and 32 named FP32 register updates (496 explicit FMAs per row). Exact-sm_103a NVCC compiled with 40 registers, zero stack/spills. Broker-shared B300 eight-chunk output check passed all 2,097,152 BF16 updates versus an independent CPU serial solve, max abs 0.00390625, inputs unchanged and lease released. This is a primitive, not KDA state recurrence.

The same native solve probe passed a full 256-chunk B300 broker-shared check on qualified P and deterministic FP32 RHS: all 67,108,864 BF16 update elements, zero tolerance/nonfinite failures, max abs 0.00390625, immutable P/RHS unchanged and released lease. This establishes full-shape primitive correctness only; RHS is synthetic and no recurrent state or public KDA output is evaluated here.

Broker-exclusive five-round x25 strict CUPTI cold-L2/no-graph timing of the correctness-qualified full native solve primitive measured 668.229 us median of round medians, max within-round CV 0.285%, one CUDA activity, finite output and immutable inputs; lease released. The primitive alone exceeds the earlier approximately 456 us complete adapted-reference diagnostic in another job. Adding its standalone duration to the separately measured 389.507 us preparation is not a valid paired full-kernel estimate, but it rules out treating a language switch alone as enough headroom.
